title: Duane "Keffe D" Davis sentenced to 40 years for rapper Tupac Shakur's murder
description: Shakur's sister, Sekyiwa Shakur, told the court: "The loss of Tupac, for a long time, crippled my family.""He had so much promise, intentions for a be
body: Shakur's sister, Sekyiwa Shakur, told the court: "The loss of Tupac, for a long time, crippled my family.""He had so much promise, intentions for a better world," said adding that her brother had hoped to help his local community. Sekyiwa Shakur asked the judge to give Davis the maximum sentence, telling Davis he will sit in prison and "contemplate what you've done to the world, not just to me".Shakur's brother, Maurice Shakur, also addressed the court, asking the judge for "the longest possible sentence".Davis was asked by Judge Carli Kierny if he had anything to say, to which he replied: "I'm good. I'm gonna appeal this case for sure."Before handing down the sentence, Kierny told him: "You don't get to take a man from his family."You don't get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur. The world never forgot about him and his death."The key evidence in the case were Davis' own words, in which he repeatedly and publicly acknowledged being inside the white Cadillac from where the deadly shots were fired.In exchange for being shielded from criminal prosecution, he told authorities about his role in Shakur's death during a secret 2008 police interview relating to the death of fellow rapper Notorious B.I.G., real name Christopher Wallace, who was killed in a shooting just months after Shakur. Davis elaborated further on his role in his 2019 memoir, Compton Street Legend, which led to publicity and media interviews. But the book and interviews he offered elaborating on his role in Shakur's killing voided a protective agreement he had established with authorities that had blocked any criminal charges from being filed. A judge then allowed his police interview to be used in the murder trial against him.Shakur was 25 years old and at the height of his career as one of rap's most influential voices at the time of his death. He has sold more than 75 million records worldwide.For three decades, the investigation into his killing remained one of America's most famous cold cases, spurring countless conspiracies - until the conviction of Davis last month.Throughout the trial, Davis' defence team tried to persuade jurors that his comments were fiction - bravado and exaggeration intended to sell books and make money.Prosecutors argued that although Davis, a former leader of the South Side Compton Crips street gang, did not himself fire the gun, he ordered the shooting and supplied the gun that his nephew Orlando Anderson used to open fire.Anderson died in an unrelated shooting in 1998, having denied involvement in the killing of Shakur.

schema.headline: Duane "Keffe D" Davis sentenced to 40 years for rapper Tupac Shakur's murder

title: Cornell cancels fraternity parties over sexual assault case
description: "It is clear that women on our campus continue to question whether they are safe. We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short
body: "It is clear that women on our campus continue to question whether they are safe. We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short and taking meaningful action," he added. Fraternities have existed at university campuses across the US for decades and function as all-male social clubs where the students live, study and socialise. Over the years, the groups have become notorious for binge-drinking, partying and dangerous hazing rituals. In a statement, a lawyer representing Doe said she filed a civil lawsuit "to achieve her aim of improving Cornell and its response to abuse claims"."While the steps announced today are helpful to achieve this goal, they are too late to protect Ms. Doe," said lawyer Thomas Giuffra. Cornell's president said anyone who violated the new fraternity party policy at the New York university would be suspended. The school also said it planned to improve support for survivors of sexual assault, including more staff to help people report sexual misconduct and navigate other support systems as well.Through Title IX, the federal law that governs how universities handle sexual assault claims, schools are required to provide measures of support to help survivors stay in school after assaults. Doe's lawyer has said she dropped out after the alleged assault. Cornell case highlights 'draining' maze for victims to report campus sex assaultsThe president said the school will allow New York State Police's trauma-informed officers to investigate allegations of sexual assault on its campus. These officers will interview survivors who want to pursue criminal charges and prepare "comprehensive investigative summaries for the appropriate law enforcement agency", Kotlikoff said. Cornell has faced criticism over the information shared with the local district attorney's office about Jane Doe's allegations. Out of hundreds of documents that US media outlets have obtained from Cornell's investigation into the assault, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said that in 2024, his office received only a six-page statement signed by the victim as well as Snapchat messages in which the men at the fraternity party advertised a free sexual encounter with Doe. State officials have also criticised Van Houten's decision not to bring charges or interview victims and witnesses himself. New York Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed the state's attorney general, Letitia James, to investigate the case. Kotlikoff said Cornell would be bringing in national sexual violence prevention experts to examine "the factors leading to campus sexual violence and strategies to promote responsible sexual citizenship".He said the steps were the first toward "systematic change" on campus.

schema.headline: Cornell cancels fraternity parties over sexual assault case

title: Royal Mail losing 400 postal workers a week, says union
description: About 400 postmen and women are leaving Royal Mail per week, according to the Communication Workers Union (CWU), who claims this number has gone up si
body: About 400 postmen and women are leaving Royal Mail per week, according to the Communication Workers Union (CWU), who claims this number has gone up since the company introduced a new delivery system earlier this year.The CWU says the firm had been losing about 330 postal staff a week from a workforce of 83,000 before it rolled out DM26, which reorganised routes to improve delivery performance.The union claims the new system is not working in hundreds of offices, and BBC Your Voice has heard from staff warning of a "nightmare" Christmas ahead as the number of parcels increases.Royal Mail says the reforms are part of its plan to deliver a more "efficient and financially sustainable" service.Over the last year we've been in touch with more than 30 postal staff in all four nations of the UK, as they have switched over to DM26.It allows for second class post to only be delivered every other weekday, and is supposed to guarantee first class mail and parcels are delivered every day, by putting workers into groups of three and changing the walking pattern of rounds.But posties speaking to us anonymously say parcels are still being prioritised, letters left behind, and time wasted in sorting and dividing mail into first and second class."I didn't take any first class mail out on my last shift because I was on a road that's been behind for weeks," a worker in the West Midlands told me. "But I'm sure a manager would have ticked a box to say all first class mail went out."A Royal Mail spokesperson said the company always worked to ensure all mail - both letters and parcels - were delivered on time.So far DM26 has been introduced in about 1,000 of Royal Mail's 1,200 delivery offices.Now the CWU has told its members to pause further roll-out of the new system until a plan can be agreed with Royal Mail to address problems.The union says that while it is operating successfully in around 500 offices, it has run into significant problems in hundreds of others."Put simply, if a boat is already taking on water, adding more passengers is unlikely to solve the problem," says Martin Walsh of the CWU.The union said most Royal Mail workers leaving the company were believed to be new starters on part-time contracts, but also said there had been an increase in staff on legacy contracts departing.Royal Mail, on the other hand, says the new system is on track to be up and running in all offices by Christmas. It says the roll-out is 90% complete and that it is now delivering to "95% of addresses every day across the UK, up from 88% before the roll-out. The roll-out continues across our network and we expect quality of service to improve as deployment progresses."The company says it is hiring, as usual, an additional 22,000 temporary workers over the Christmas period.Royal Mail has battled with increased competition and falling demand for letter deliveries in recent years, and last week announced plans to cut 2,500 head office and other supporting roles by the end of 2027.The company has also faced years of criticism from politicians and the public over slow letter deliveries - something which has continued since the new system has been rolled out.The regulator Ofcom has fined Royal Mail more than £37m in the last three years for missing delivery targets. But some MPs think it is time for a new approach, and a group of them will meet the regulator later on Wednesday."We need to think outside the box," Dave Robertson, Labour MP for Lichfield, Burntwood and the Villages in Staffordshire. "We need to bring as many people to the table on this to make sure we come up with a long-term solution because what's been tried up to now clearly isn't working."An Ofcom spokesperson said not only has it issued fines to Royal Mail in recent years but it has also demanded an improvement plan and reformed the obligations imposed on the company, adding: "We will continue to hold it to account using the full extent of the powers available to us."Postal Services Minister Kate Dearden said Royal Mail's improvement plan was "a step in the right direction, but it must deliver tangible improvements for customers. We will continue to hold them to account on their performance."

schema.headline: Royal Mail losing 400 postal workers a week, says union

title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF
description: There is increased concern about how much money countries are borrowing, but the IMF said the UK is doing better than all other major economies at thi
body: There is increased concern about how much money countries are borrowing, but the IMF said the UK is doing better than all other major economies at this.The IMF said the UK "basically stands out, along with India" when it comes to addressing the problem and by 2031 it is projected to have the lowest annual borrowing of the G7 group of countries, which includes Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the US.Sir Howard Davies, former deputy governor of the Bank of England, said this was largely because the UK has a government with a majority which has committed to tackling the situation, which it is expected to achieve either through tax rises, cuts to public services, or a mix of both.By contrast, he says the US has said little about reducing its deficit, while France and Germany don't have majority governments."So, we [the UK] are not great students, but we look somewhat better than some of the others we are sharing the class with," he said.Meanwhile, the IMF's growth forecasts for the UK mean it is expected to have the second-fastest growing economy in the G7 this year along with Germany.Sir Howard believes this should also be seen in context."We're still growing slowly. It's almost like saying we're winning a slow bicycle race here because other people are going backwards a bit more rapidly than we are."

schema.headline: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

title: Bumble bought for $1.3bn in 'bet on the future of humanity'
description: Dating app Bumble has been bought for $1.3bn (£980m) in what the new owners called "a bet on the future of humanity". Investment firm Ithaca Holdings
body: Dating app Bumble has been bought for $1.3bn (£980m) in what the new owners called "a bet on the future of humanity". Investment firm Ithaca Holdings is taking over the loss-making firm and it directors, Ravi Gupta and John Hegeman, will become co-chief executives of the company which once differentiated itself by having a "women-first" chat rule.Bumble ditched the rule in August this year.Whitney Wolfe Herd, Bumble's founder and current chief executive, said she would remain "actively involved" with the business she set up 12 years ago.While it is unclear what Wolfe Herd's role at the dating app will be, she said she will work closely with the new owners. Gupta and Hegeman said they wanted to use technology to "renew and accelerate businesses...in a world transformed by AI".They said: "Technology should work in service of our deepest source of fulfillment, human connection and this investment is a bet on the future of humanity."This contrasts with a recent debate over the safety of AI, with some experts claiming the speed of its development threatens the future of humanity. Bumble's share price has soared as news of the deal began to emerge. The jump lifted its company valuation to over $580m but that is still far below a peak of more than $14bn it reached after it floated the business on the Nasdaq stock index in 2021.Since becoming a public company, it has made an annual pre-tax profit only once, in 2023.In the following two years, it reported steep losses, though during that period Bumble had been working to incorporate new technology, including AI, into its app.Its chief executive in 2024, Lidiane Jones, told the BBC she believed AI had "exciting potential" in dating apps related to safety, and Bumble had been looking at research that found Gen Z and milliennials were interested in AI assistance with creating profiles.This year, the dating app unveiled several new AI features, including profile guidance to help people create dating profiles. Bumble was launched in 2014 by Wolfe Herd who built the brand around a distinctive feature that only allowed women to initiate conversations with matches.It recently abandoned that rule, prompting debate among users over whether the app had lost what set it apart from rivals."Today, our community is asking for more flexibility, less pressure, and more opportunities to create real, meaningful connections and that is what this new experience provides," Wolfe Herd said in August.Dating apps like Bumble have come under pressure in recent years as some younger users have grown disillusioned with browsing for dates.Bumble said in 2025 that it would cut almost a third of its workforce as the industry grappled with what Wolfe Herd described as an "inflection point" in online dating.Investments in other dating companies have also soured as apps have struggled to convince users to pay for their services.Match Group - which owns apps including Tinder, OkCupid and Hinge - has also seen its shares fall sharply from their peak in 2021.According to a report by media watchdog Ofcom in 2025, adults in the UK were spending less time on dating apps compared to three years earlier.Some single people are instead turning to board game get-togethers, book clubs and other group activities in the hope of finding a partner.

schema.headline: Bumble bought for $1.3bn in 'bet on the future of humanity'

title: Saudi employee charged with planting recording device at OpenAI office
description: A Saudi national has been charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's offices in California, federal prosecutors announced. A
body: A Saudi national has been charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's offices in California, federal prosecutors announced. Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked at the AI firm as an engineer, was charged federally with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications.OpenAI said it had discovered a "sophisticated recording device" hidden in their San Francisco office and alerted the FBI. The company said it used its AI models to track that it had been planted by an employee.Prosecutors say the device, wrapped in toilet paper, was found inserted in a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room. OpenAI, the maker of the popular chatbot ChatGPT, said that it has no indication that source code, model weights or customer data were inappropriately accessed or taken in the incident. It said the employee has been fired. According to the complaint, Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement.Patel said that the alleged goal was to capture information about the company's AI product.Alfozan has been working as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, prosecutors say.On 30 September, OpenAI employees discovered the device - two days after prosecutors say it had been installed. The device was encrypted, prosecutors said.OpenAI said they were able to use their AI models "to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier". According to the FBI, the suspect used a "productivity tool" and a "chatbot" to research sensitive locations at OpenAI and how to secretly place audio equipment.Chatbot prompts that he is alleged to have searched include "building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device", prosecutors allege. He is also accused of using the chatbot to ask about "'build[ing] a continuous audio recorder,' 'customiz[ing] Wi-Fi . . . connectivity,' 'improv[ing] audio and live listening,' and 'encrypt[ing] the SD card'".

schema.headline: Saudi employee charged with planting recording device at OpenAI office

title: What we know about the man who died falling from a Six Flags rollercoaster
description: The Cobb County Police Department said the incident at the Six Flags Over Georgia park happened just before 16:00 local time (20:00 GMT) on Monday."Of
body: The Cobb County Police Department said the incident at the Six Flags Over Georgia park happened just before 16:00 local time (20:00 GMT) on Monday."Officers working at the park responded to an incident involving a male guest on a roller coaster," it said in a statement on Tuesday."Preliminary information gathered through witness and employee interview indicates Kariem was ejected from the ride and struck other patrons before falling beneath the attraction."The ride involved has not been specified but aerial footage from news helicopters showed the Goliath rollercoaster stopped midway, and multiple witnesses have identified the ride as the one involved in the incident. The office of the state's insurance and fire safety commissioner, which enforces amusement park safety rules in Georgia, is also conducting a review.Officials have not held a news conference on the incident.The Goliath ride opened in 2006, and it has an elevation of 200ft (60m), a 170ft plunge, a 540-degree spiral, and a speed of up to 70mph (112km/h), according to the park website. On its "thrill scale", Six Flags ranks Goliath at level four out of five.The company said in a statement that it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident" and that "our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones".Nick Mendenhall said he witnessed the fatal moments in disbelief, watching the man come out of his seat and then fall into another cart on the ride before falling to the ground. "It was just super, super bizarre, traumatic. I mean, it took me a couple of seconds, I feel like, to process what was going on," he told the AP. "I cant believe that I just saw that."He said his mind instantly went to the trauma of all of those impacted by what he witnessed, including the man's loved ones and everyone who was on the ride with him. One witness told NBC affiliate WXIA that the incident was captured in souvenir photos that were automatically taken of the rollercoaster while it was in motion. The BBC has not been able to verify this statement. Connor Thompson told the BBC's US partner CBS News that he was in line for the ride when everyone started "yelling, clearly distressed". "Everyone was kind of confused at first, and then there was someone who was  yelling, 'Call 911! Someone fell out!" he said. "At first it was almost like I didn't believe it because I thought that was like impossible for something like that to happen." He said he saw the cart come into the hub where others were waiting in line and could see the restraint was unlatched. Another witness, CiCi Nelson, told CNN she, too, was in line to ride the Goliath when the rollercoaster returned and she saw an empty seat with a loose safety bar and a female covered in blood.Nelson described a scene of hysteria, adding that one man was "freaking out, saying someone fell off".Brittany Landry, who believed she saw Kariem ejected from the rollercoaster, told Fox News she was in tears."I broke because we were just on there," she said.Kariem's family said he was a father, passionate educator and had survived two bouts of cancer.His family told WXIA that he had survived cancer twice - the last stint in 2018 - and was in a car crash with his 10-year-old daughter three weeks before his death. He lived in the nearby city of Atlanta and worked for Wesley International Academy, a public charter school, for more than 12 years as an IT manager, technology teacher and robotics coach."Mr. Kariem was deeply loved and respected, and his absence will be felt throughout our school community," the school said in a statement posted to its Facebook account."His love for Wesley, dedication to our students, and commitment to our school community were evident in everything he did."Outside of work, Kariem enjoyed creating products with his laser engraver and 3D printers, as well as cooking, watching anime and spending time with family and friends, according to his profile on the school's website.The death at Six Flags Over Georgia is at least the seventh there, according to the Doan Law Firm, which tracks amusement park accidents and represents victims.According to the firm, this includes two people who had medical emergencies, two who were in restricted areas when they were struck by a ride, two who died in car-related accidents and one who died months after using the park's pool.Six Flags operates 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resorts across Canada, the US and Mexico.In the last 15 years, two deaths caused by falling from the park's rollercoasters led to lawsuits and settlements. One in 2011 involved an Iraq War veteran who was ejected from a ride in New York and hit his head on the car. In the other, in 2013, a woman slipped from her restraints on a rollercoaster in Texas and fell 75 feet. In September, the Six Flags Magic Mountain park in California announced it was closing its X2 rollercoaster after more 100 people alleged that they had suffered brain injuries from the ride.With additional reporting by Brandon Drenon

schema.headline: What we know about the man who died falling from a Six Flags rollercoaster

title: Women's World Cup play-offs: 'Unplayable' Georgia Stanway proves a 'warrior' for England
description: Stanway's strikes in the last five days capped off a season in which she finished as England's top scorer and netted 11 times in her last 11 matches.S
body: Stanway's strikes in the last five days capped off a season in which she finished as England's top scorer and netted 11 times in her last 11 matches.She also ranks inside the top three for most goals scored by European players in international football since Euro 2025.While Wiegman was frustrated by her side's lack of ruthlessness in Greece, Stanway always looked dangerous and made sure she got on the scoresheet.It felt inevitable she would join in the fun in Leicester when Alessia Russo and Lauren James grabbed a double each.Stanway came close to matching them when the Arsenal midfielder coolly took control of a long ball inside the box with one deft touch and, with the second, fired it powerfully into the bottom corner.It would have been the perfect strike to mark an impressive few days but it was ruled out for offside, much to Wiegman's dismay."She is always so eager to go towards goal. She has that tenacity in her," said the England boss when asked about Stanway's goalscoring form."She is always aggressive out of possession but also in possession. She scored a great header and controlled that really good ball from Alex Greenwood."That was really good athleticism and composure. Unfortunately that was disallowed but it was really good! "Football is about scoring goals, but also playing in the pockets, keeping the ball and connecting with other players - and I was happy with her [doing those]."Former England goalkeeper Rachel Brown-Finnis told BBC Radio 5 Live that Stanway was "unplayable at times" against Greece on Tuesday night.She won all her tackles, had a 90% passing accuracy rate, took four shots, scored once and had another disallowed.It was also a slightly different role for Stanway for most of the match as she played more as a right winger after changes in the midfield."She has something different to others," Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live."She is goal-orientated, has a great shot and the disallowed goal showed her great mobility and athleticism."When you really need a fight, or a duel, or a counter-attack breaking up, she is there. She is a warrior who you can play a possession game with too."Stanway was even more effective in large part to a new-look midfield which included 20-year-old debutant Lexi Potter.The Chelsea midfielder provided cover for the experienced Stanway and Keira Walsh to push higher up, while Lauren James played in the number 10 role.It proved to be an inspired change from Wiegman as Stanway caused problems throughout for the visitors and was able to adapt to the tweaks impressively."Stanway has shown how flexible she is, how exceptional she is both at the bottom end of the pitch, breaking up play, as well as at the top end," added Brown-Finnis. "She was playing as a second striker, playing out on the right, dropping deep as a number 10. She's been absolutely brilliant."England still have a job to do to qualify for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil with a two-legged play-off tie against Ukraine to navigate at the end of the year.They have already beaten their opponents 9-1 on aggregate in two games of the league phase of the qualifiers.After Wiegman's formation experiment worked so well this week, could it be an option for the future that brings out the best in Stanway, as well as others?"I liked the balance of the midfield. There is a lot of competition going on in that area," admitted Wiegman."There were a few reasons. First of all, I wanted to see Lexi Potter deeper on the pitch and what that might bring. "There was also the option to put Georgia Stanway higher up the pitch. We wanted to score more goals and we know that she can do that. "She can play in the pocket and also deeper on the pitch so we wanted to see all of that."

schema.headline: Women's World Cup play-offs: 'Unplayable' Georgia Stanway proves a 'warrior' for England

title: RJ Mitte: How Breaking Bad star changed the way we see cerebral palsy
description: Figure caption, 'Disabled or not, everyone deserves an opportunity,' RJ Mitte says in 2015 BBC interviewByEmma SaundersCulture reporter"I have cerebra
body: Figure caption, 'Disabled or not, everyone deserves an opportunity,' RJ Mitte says in 2015 BBC interviewByEmma SaundersCulture reporter"I have cerebral palsy but I've never let it hold me back."Those are the words of a 22-year-old Breaking Bad star RJ Mitte in an essay for Huffpost, external back in 2014.Explaining his experiences of learning to stand up to bullies while growing up, he added: "It shouldn't define you. I just happen to have CP."That was also true of Mitte's character Walter 'Flynn' White Jr, the son of Bryan Cranston's character in the drama, which was recently named the best TV show of the 21st Century by the New York Times."What I really like is that he was on TV playing a character that had cerebral palsy, but it wasn't about the fact that he had cerebral palsy," says Emma Livingstone, founder and CEO of Up - the Adult Cerebral Palsy Movement."When we see RJ Mitte on TV just playing a role, but who also happens to have CP, I think that's really powerful."Mitte, who died by suicide on Monday at the age of 34, wasn't just an actor - he was also an advocate and supporter, working as an ambassador for charities including United Cerebral Palsy and Can Do Canines, as well as creating The Mitte Foundation, which offered community grants in his home town in Texas.Image source, Getty ImagesSusan Sellers, president and CEO of United Cerebral Palsy, says: "His advocacy was rooted in a commitment to ensuring that people with cerebral palsy and other disabilities are seen, heard, and afforded the opportunity to reach their full potential."Mitte's legacy, particularly for performers with disabilities, is significant.Ruth Madeley, who stars as disability rights advocate Judy Heumann in new film Being Heumann, tells the BBC: "If you don't see it, you don't think it's possible. When I was younger, acting wasn't even on my radar. I didn't even think it was an option."The actress, who has spina bifida, adds: "To have people like him [Mitte] on screen for so many young people looking at the arts as an industry that they want to get into... He was just a beautiful example of that."But he wasn't just a disabled person breaking down barriers in the industry. He was a phenomenal talent, and I think that's what's going to be missed so much."Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Mitte was mobbed by fans on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2013Another actor, Keron Day, who appeared in Netflix hit Sex Education, tells the BBC: "My biggest tribute I can pay to RJ and his work is that I am emailing you today from a set of a TV show."That is his legacy: disabled people having careers within the creative industries. If I could have half the impact that RJ has had, I would be enormously proud. It's a sad day for both our industry and our community."Comedian and screenwriter Laurence Clarke concurs. "The more portrayals that we see on TV, that's going to inspire more disabled people to think it's a career for them," he says."Things have moved on a long way since Breaking Bad came out in 2008. But there's always further to go."Speaking of Mitte's role in Breaking Bad, Clarke tells the BBC: "What's beautiful about it is that the disability is visibly there, always."He also notes the impact on people watching inclusive dramas and shows."The more you're exposed to those portrayals, as members of the public, it becomes just part of life, and how you see the world."Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Bryan Cranston (left) played RJ Mitte's dad in the hugely successful Breaking BadMitte was aged three when he was diagnosed with cerebral palsy, which the NHS describes as the name for a group of lifelong conditions that affect movement and co-ordination caused by a problem with the brain that develops around birth.He was cast in Breaking Bad at 14, and told Channel 4 News in 2016 that the show "pioneered a lot of TV and writers to be more brave".But he added a note of caution, saying: "We still have a long way to go... it's still a business and we have to do that slowly."Earlier this month, he hinted that he may be interested in continuing the Breaking Bad story, external, but said any revival would have a lot to live up to."I just want to top Breaking Bad, that's the hardest," he said. "I set a bar for myself as a young man that is kinda unattainable. I tell people, 'Look, it's a long way down from the top of the mountain'."After Breaking Bad, Mitte's other on-screen credits include Hannah Montana, Switched at Birth, Westhampton and his latest project, Talking to Strangers, which came out earlier this year.But his biggest achievement - and his greatest pride - was his philanthropic work."Where I felt most top of the world was being able to help others through Breaking Bad, with the work I've done with people with disabilities... trying to remind people they have a voice and [to] lend my voice."The greatest thing that Breaking Bad has given me is to be able to lend my voice to causes that make a meaningful impact, that change people's lives."

schema.headline: RJ Mitte: How Breaking Bad star changed the way we see cerebral palsy

title: African Grand Prix: Why Rwanda has been chosen to host Formula 1
description: Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali hailed the new deal to take the sport back to Africa - ending an absence of nearly 40 years - as a "landmark" a
body: Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali hailed the new deal to take the sport back to Africa - ending an absence of nearly 40 years - as a "landmark" achievement.Lewis Hamilton has been pushing the importance of having a grand prix in Africa for some time.But the sport's bosses already recognised the importance of the project. And this deal marks the end of nearly 10 years of effort by F1's owners Liberty Media, which has had an ambition to hold a race in Africa since it bought the sport at the start of 2017.Rwanda, which has signed a 10-year deal to host an African Grand Prix from the "early 2030s", has succeeded where Morocco and South Africa, among others, have failed.That's because the east-central African country has managed to put together a single plan with the requisite financial backing and ambition to make the project work.Morocco never found the finances and South Africa has up to four separate projects ongoing with different promoters in three different locations, two in Cape Town. For F1, with other countries also interested in slots on an already crowded schedule, that was too much to deal with.The new Rwandan circuit being built in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital Kigali, is part of a wider development near a new international airport, currently under construction, that also includes facilities in sectors such as entertainment, residential, hotels, spas and sports science, as well as an innovation hub.At the moment it is a greenfield site, but insiders say there should be no difficulties completing the project by 2030.The race is likely to be controversial as Rwanda has previously been accused of sportswashing.But for Domenicali the deal marks a key moment in the sport's development under his leadership."It is the legacy of all of us to be in this very special moment," he said as he took the stage at the announcement in Kigali with Rwandan President Paul Kagame and FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem.He added that he was "very proud", and that F1 was "showing the world what it means to be a country that has a vision"."Rwanda is one of the world's great success stories," he said. "A nation of extraordinary natural beauty and stunning landscapes, combined with resilience and courage to overcome and be reborn from challenges of its past."It is a nation filled with ambition, creativity and determination. A nation that has become a destination for international investment, innovation and opportunity."From a purely sporting point of view, it's easy to see why Domenicali is so chuffed.He has brought F1 back to Africa, where the last grand prix was held in 1993 in South Africa, and opened up a potential market of 100 million people that is largely untapped.And the track, designed by former F1 driver Alex Wurz, promises a great deal.Wurz is passionate about creating circuits with natural flow that challenge drivers, and he has envisaged this one in the style of the classic Spa-Francorchamps, Suzuka and Mugello tracks, with its own unique character - and the renders released do bear some obvious similarities to the first part of Suzuka.The track is not completely finalised - there will be further consultation with teams and drivers - but is envisaged to be about 6km (3.7 miles) long, with 17 corners, and will use the undulating Rwandan landscape to help create a dramatic layout. It has nearly 200m of elevation change.President Kagame has backed this project as a way of showcasing his country on the global stage, saying it would bring "jobs, skills, tourism and new business" to Africa.Kagame said he wanted to "pave the way for other races to be hosted on the continent", and that projects such as this act as a catalyst to "help break the cycle" of African athletes achieving on the world stage but the continent getting little in return."We are not just looking at Rwanda alone," he said. "We are looking at Rwanda in the context of a continent and we have ambitions to bring in our African brothers and sisters to participate. We have had many other big events."Rwanda is fighting off any allegations that the project is using money that would be better directed elsewhere, in a country that receives international aid, by emphasising that the funding is coming from a newly established development fund combining public and private investment.Last month, it launched a five-year plan aiming to attract £3.5bn in private investment to accelerate Rwanda's economic transformation and expansion.The grand prix is part of the country's wider strategy to increase tourism, international investment, services and entertainment, bringing more prospects to the country and further growing the overall GDP of the nation.But Rwanda is not the first country to want to use F1 in this way. And the use of sport to build a country's image can, depending on context, be viewed in a less positive light, as sportswashing - the use of major sports events to distract from aspects of the country's conduct that parts of the wider international community find problematic.The F1 calendar already contains a number of countries that fall into this category, not least Saudi Arabia.Rwanda is the subject of a case brought by its neighbour, the Democratic Republic of Congo, at the International Court of Justice, accusing it of breaching multiple international treaties covering genocide prevention, racial discrimination, women's rights and torture.F1 is far from the only sport to face such accusations. They have been levelled at Premier League football clubs Arsenal and Aston Villa as a consequence of sponsorship deals with Rwanda.Saudi Arabia will host the Fifa World Cup in 2034. Boxing has become heavily reliant on Saudi Arabian finance. Golf came close to being torn apart by Saudi money and the establishment of the rival LIV tour.F1 is not blind to such issues. Its own charter commits it to "respecting internationally recognised human rights in its operations globally" and emphasises the importance of understanding and monitoring potential human rights impacts and engaging with stakeholders to address any issues that arise.It also says it focuses its efforts "in relation to those areas which are within our own direct influence".A statement in the context of the Rwandan announcement said: "We have the opportunity to inspire and bring the passion of F1 to 100 million people across Africa and sport can be a positive force for good."But Felix Jakens, Amnesty International UK's head of campaigns, said: "Rwanda is buying into the world's biggest sports to polish its image and deflect from its appalling human rights record."Formula 1 says sport can be 'a positive force for good'. That rings hollow if F1 shrugs off who it is partnering with."Formula 1 must not be a bystander. It should use its influence with the Rwandan authorities to push for change, rather than lend its brand to a PR exercise."

schema.headline: African Grand Prix: Why Rwanda has been chosen to host Formula 1

title: Independent regulator report says English football finances are 'dangerously exposed'
description: English football's finances are "dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster", according to a landmark re
body: English football's finances are "dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster", according to a landmark report by the independent football regulator.Research by the watchdog found 94% of clubs are loss-making, and more than 60% of EFL and National League clubs are technically insolvent.The regulator (IFR) warns of "a dangerous cocktail of rising debt and an over-reliance on owner funding, leaving clubs and their fans at risk".The 'State of the Game' report also suggests that despite the economic success of the Premier League, the financial 'cliff-edges' between and within leagues have grown significantly.The report says: 94% of clubs in the top five English leagues made losses in 2025-2617 clubs across the EFL and National League would be loss-making even if their players played for free66% of clubs could not survive for more than 90 days without new owner funding29% of clubs reported they could not survive more than 30 days without such funding68% of clubs have no contingency plan if their owner walks away The IFR claims "the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform", and its report "should serve as a wake-up call" for English football."Seventeen clubs are now trading in such a way that if their players played for free, their non-playing costs would mean they would go bust," IFR chair David Kogan told BBC Sport."Thirty-two clubs are operating on only 30 days' cash. If the owner chooses not to pay cash at the end of the month, those clubs go bust."That is a very, very risky scenario. This is the moment of addressing these problems before money starts to dry up. "We can actually fix the house while the sun is still shining and that's essentially what our role is going to be in this."Tasked with improving teams' financial sustainability, the IFR outlined six areas of concern around financial risk, and urged clubs to put robust contingency plans in place in case owner funding is withdrawn.Despite years of talks, the Premier League and EFL are yet to agree a new funding settlement that would see the top flight share more money with the rest of the pyramid. The IFR has the power to impose a deal and warns that "if football can't find a solution we will consider our next steps and will not hesitate to use all the powers at our disposal to bring about lasting change".It also urges action on rising losses and calls on clubs to show how they take fans' views into account, and the steps they are taking to improve boardroom diversity and governance.The report also found:The average Premier League club now earns more than eight times the average Championship sideThe existing system of parachute payments paid by the Premier League to Championship clubs who have been relegated "contributes to the incentives for Championship clubs to overspend which drives up player wage inflation"Net transfer debt is going up and deferred transfer payments and transfer financing create links between clubs, owners and lenders which increases "the potential for financial stress to spread across the game"."Nobody in football for 100 years has believed that football was trading in a solvent and effective state," Kogan said. "It's not how football has ever really operated. "But I think now where there's so much more money involved, the extremes get more extreme. "We knew the problems were there, I don't think anybody realised that the data was going to show quite how dramatic they are."The Premier League, the EFL, the Football Association and the Football Supporters' Association have all issued statements welcoming the findings.BBC Sport outlines some of the key points in the report. The report says the financial situation is worsening for clubs across the EFL and National League.Most Championship, League One and League Two clubs hold less than 30 days of cash. More than 60% of EFL and National League clubs have liabilities exceeding the book value of their assets.It is a bleak picture for wages, too.Twenty clubs - primarily in the Championship, League One and National League -spent more than 80% of revenue on player wages.The majority of League One clubs spend more than 40% of revenue on player wages, including two spending more than 100%.Wage costs have increased across all leagues between 2021-22 and 2025-26:33% in the Premier League32% in the Championship71% in League One63% in League TwoSeventeen of 18 (94%) EFL club owners surveyed were in favour of more robust cost controls - as one investor told the report: "the single biggest issue is player wages".Average League One losses increased from 6% of revenue in 1992-93 to almost 50% in 2024-25. In League Two, it stands at 40%.Many clubs rely on owner funding on a just-in-time basis, receiving frequent injections throughout the year.The majority of EFL and National League clubs do not have a contingency plan if their owner becomes unable or unwilling to continue financing operations.This leaves them particularly exposed given their limited access to alternative sources of finance."League One and the League Two clubs will receive significantly more funding [through a new deal with the Premier League]," Kogan said. "That funding will be used along with a development fund and a liquidity fund potentially to help them get over the humps they're all currently facing."In respect of both liquidity and solvency, the report says many football clubs "would not currently meet the requirement under the Football Governance Act to hold 'appropriate financial resources'." Clubs are required to meet this standard by May 2030."Owners are very well aware of the need now for some sort of coherent structure in which costs are being managed," Kogan said. Kogan added that the new financial distribution deal between the Premier League and the EFL is close.It will not be news that the gap between the Premier League and the Championship has grown. In 1992-93, the average Premier League club earned £10.5m, which was 2.7 times the £3.9m earned by the average Championship club. By 2024-25 it was £341m, or 8.7 times the £38.9m in the second tier.The revenue gap within the Championship has also grown, partly because of the increase in the size of parachute payments.From 2007-08 to 2025-26, the amount a non-parachute Championship club received in solidarity payments from the Premier League increased from £0.9m to £5.3m.But a year-one parachute club saw payments increase from £12m to £48.7m.The absolute revenue gap between the big six and the rest of the Premier League has widened significantly, too.In 1992-93, the six biggest clubs in terms of revenue earned £9.4m more on average. By 2024-25, this average revenue gap had grown to £421m.The big six account for 56% Premier League revenues, with 44% split between the remaining 14 teams.

schema.headline: Independent regulator report says English football finances are 'dangerously exposed'

title: Lisandro Martinez attacks Man Utd board after Atletico Madrid defeat
description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has launched a blistering attack on the club's hierarchy for not strengthening the squad following qualif
body: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has launched a blistering attack on the club's hierarchy for not strengthening the squad following qualification for the Champions League.Tuesday's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid means United have now gone five games without a win.Their most recent victory was against Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK on 10 September. United's only other win in nine matches this season came against newly promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford, when they had to come from behind.The Red Devils finished third in the Premier League last term to seal a Champions League return for the first time in three years.They won 12 of Michael Carrick's 17 games in interim charge following the dismissal of Ruben Amorim in January, which was enough to earn the former United midfielder a permanent two-year contract as head coach."We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well," Martinez told Amazon Prime."Atletico have an amazing team and they deserved to win today."I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. "I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."Tonight it is easy to [blame] the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."Martinez's view has been echoed by many external observers and has also been mentioned by some inside Old Trafford.The failure to bring in striking support for Benjamin Sesko and competition at left-back for Luke Shaw have both been highlighted in a summer when United spent £155m on three midfielders to the exclusion of any other position.Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was sitting next to United chief executive Omar Berrada in the Metropolitano Stadium on Tuesday.They have sacked managers in the past two seasons after backing them the previous summer, with Erik ten Hag dismissed in October 2024, before Amorim was shown the exit door in January 2026."You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager," said Martinez. "What about other areas? I can't say more."Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team."Martinez's comments echo similar ones made by his Argentina defensive partner Cristian Romero against the Tottenham board last season. Ironically, Romero was in Atletico's side against United after his summer move to Spain.Martinez, meanwhile, has one year left on his United contract and has yet to agree an extension.Former United players Wayne Rooney and Ashley Young were in Madrid for the game.Discussing Martinez's comments on Amazon Prime, both said the defender had gone too far and the damage inside the dressing room could be significant."Something like that will rip that dressing room apart," said Rooney.The former England and United captain recalled his own public criticism of the club in 2010 which drew a fierce response from boss Sir Alex Ferguson.Rooney said it had been a mistake which he had apologised for."It is disrespectful to his team-mates," he said. "He is saying his team-mates aren't good enough."Bruno [Fernandes] is the only one with any right to say that. Behind closed doors, it happens - but that interview isn't going to help..."[Martinez] has tried to speak on behalf of the players but done it the wrong way."It looks like a player trying to look after himself. It was very premeditated. It is sad because you need everyone to stick together, you need to be as one."Tielemans - who United bought from Aston Villa for £35m in July - also spoke to the host broadcaster but opted not to respond to the question.Commentating on the game, and speaking before Martinez, former England striker Alan Shearer said he felt Carrick had been let down.Young feels Martinez should have kept his counsel."We know recruitment has to work and be better but players have to be better," he said. "They are the ones who have to produce. "There's going to be no change now. That could create [issues] all week after what was a good performance."Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, former England keeper Paul Robinson said he could understand Martinez's point."I question his timing because with the noise around Manchester United at the moment, positivity needs to come out of the dressing room," he said."But on the flip side, I actually quite like it - a player being honest. "Manchester United fans don't need their players coming out saying 'we're doing OK, the squad's strong enough'."Everyone can see they didn't recruit well enough and they need more players and the squad's not strong enough."Although United were much improved on their tepid display against Tottenham at the weekend, conceding inside the first minute did not reflect well on Carrick.And they have now gone five games without a win for the first time since 2024-25, when it happened under both Ten Hag and Amorim. Carrick remains under intense pressure, although Martinez's words will bring renewed focus on Wilcox.The former Southampton executive's appointment as football director is starting to be questioned, as are decisions taken by Ratcliffe and Berrada since the Glazer family stepped back despite remaining as majority shareholders.In addition to sacking Ten Hag and Amorim, they also dismissed highly respected Dan Ashworth in December 2024 just five months after his appointment as sporting director.Ratcliffe has also been blamed for increasing ticket prices and launching what the club said was a ticket touting investigation among season ticket holders, but which fans felt was an attempt to drive them out in favour of 'tourist' supporters.In their latest set of accounts, United's overall debt stood at £1.1bn, with some fans criticising the decision to spend £63.5m on land for a new 100,000-capacity stadium - which is set to cost in excess of £2bn - rather than use the money to strengthen Carrick's squad.United have only qualified for the Champions League in successive seasons twice sinceFerguson retired in 2013.Amorim told Wilcox to concentrate on his own job in a blistering final news conference as United boss, when he suggested too much attention was paid to external "noise" from the likes of ex-player Gary Neville.Carrick was initially asked for his response to Martinez's remarks live on TV, before heading to the post-match news conference where he was questioned about the comments by three different reporters."I haven't seen the interview," he said. "I've half heard about it. It's a bit about the emotions of the game."Straight after the game is not the time to talk about that interview and I can't really comment on that. It's important for us to move forward quickly."As group, I don't doubt the togetherness and us wanting to win. I know results-wise, it's easy to look and think there's something deeply wrong, but the players have been great in their willing."Asked if he would speak to Martinez about his comments, Carrick said: "I need to find out a bit more about it before I can say if and what is going to be done."Mark: Wow, very brave for Martinez for call out the upper management like that. I'm sure it won't go down well within Manchester United but I am also sure fans will be happy that someone in the club is finally saying it in public.Stuart McLean: Martinez is right, refreshing to hear an honest assessment. Rooney and Young being unhappy and 'should be kept in the boardroom' are so wrong, we pay their astronomical wages. We should praise the honesty, as we all know the problems.Ben Dutton: Martinez saying what most of the fans think. The rot starts at the top, and the squad is not up to the task. Rare honesty from a modern player!Andrew Mitchell: Might be the best thing Lisandro has done in a United shirt. But the ownership are still there against the wishes of nearly every United fan, they continue to run the club the way they want (to its detriment), so there's no need to think Martinez's words will move them.Joel Sparks: Martinez might be correct about the people at the top not doing enough. But their lack of activity is not causing his poor performances. Solanke didn't get the better of him on Saturday because of a lack of subs. He needs to give his head a wobble.Dave Barry: It feels shocking to hear Martinez speak so openly. Those are criticisms fans have been chatting about in the pub for years - hearing it from a player's mouth is staggering.

schema.headline: Lisandro Martinez attacks Man Utd board after Atletico Madrid defeat

title: MI5 chief warns against overstating Russian interference in Brexit vote
description: MI5 chief Sir Ken McCallum has said there was Russian interference in the the Brexit referendum, but warned against overstating its impact on the resu
body: MI5 chief Sir Ken McCallum has said there was Russian interference in the the Brexit referendum, but warned against overstating its impact on the result. It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham provoked a backlash from some Brexit campaigners by saying it was "clear" there had been interference by Moscow in the 2016 vote.Sir Ken said it was "a matter of public record" that there was interference in the referendum by online trolls and bots.However, he suggested Russian trolls would be "delighted" to be front page news again, "despite the comparative unimpressiveness" of their efforts. He added: "There is a really important difference between interference attempted and outcome swayed."I am a little bit anxious that we don't play into our adversaries' hands by making these trolls look 10ft tall."Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart branded Sir Ken's comments "an extraordinary slap down to the prime minister".In an interview released on Monday, Burnham told The Rest is Politics podcast, external that upon arriving in Downing Street, he had asked if there had been Russian interference in the 2016 vote, adding: "I've had the clear answer that, yes, there was."He did not provide details about the extent or nature of Russian activities during the interview, and when pressed on the subject in the House of Commons on Monday afternoon appeared to be less definitive.The PM denied claims from Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch that he was implying the referendum result was illegitimate because of Russian interference.He said it was a "matter of record" that Russia sought to interfere in the 2019 general election, adding: "We think it is inconceivable that this was the first time".A No 10 spokesperson also clarified that while the prime minister believed it was highly likely Russia tried to influence the referendum result, he did not believe those efforts were successful.The Conservatives accused Burnham of making an "embarrassing retreat" after "being caught out trying question the legitimacy of the referendum result".Answering questions after his annual speech at MI5's London headquarters earlier, Sir Ken said: "It is openly on the record that Russia Today and Sputnik and other Russian media organisations came in pretty strongly around the referendum."And it is also a matter of open source record that there was a certain amount of interference attempted through trolls and bots and so forth."He added that he agreed "strongly" with the PM that there was a hack and leak during the 2019 general election campaign.However, he raised concerns about the impact of the debate on Russian interference."It is kind of up to us how far we allow our various adversaries to divide us," Sir Ken said."And I'm a little bit worried that if we all stay in this debate for another few days, that Russian trolls who didn't appear to do all that much at various points over the years, they'll be delighted because they are front page news again despite the comparative unimpressiveness of what they do at all points along the journey."Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has accused Burnham of lying, saying there was "no Russian interference" in the referendum.Meanwhile, former Prime Minister Boris Johnson said that in 2016, when he became foreign secretary, the security services had told him "there was no evidence of any successful interference in the 2016 referendum, by Russia or any other power".He added: "Either the security services have changed their view - which would be very odd - or Burnham is lying about what he has been told."In 2020, a parliamentary report did not reach a firm conclusion on whether Russia had tried to intervene in UK elections and referendums, but criticised the government for failing to fully assess and counter the threat from Russian "troll" accounts on social media.

schema.headline: MI5 chief warns against overstating Russian interference in Brexit vote

title: Family pays tribute to 'warm and engaging' man killed in tiger attack
description: The family of a man who was killed by a tiger after he entered its enclosure at a wildlife park has paid tribute, describing him as "bright, warm and
body: The family of a man who was killed by a tiger after he entered its enclosure at a wildlife park has paid tribute, describing him as "bright, warm and engaging".William Chapman, 23, visited Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster on Saturday and was attacked after going into the animal's pen. He was pronounced dead at the scene.In a statement, his family said that he had suffered from "significant mental illness" over a number of years and had been prescribed "strong medication".It said it was for the coroner to decide whether his mental illness played a part in his death, asking that the public respect that process.City of Doncaster Council has launched a health and safety investigation into Chapman's death and the park remains closed."William was a bright, warm and engaging young man whom his family dearly loved - and William loved them back," a statement released on Tuesday evening said.The family also asked for privacy, saying "the publication and circulation of deeply offensive media content is causing them severe distress at an exceptionally vulnerable time"."The family are utterly devastated by their loss and are struggling to come to terms with what has happened," the statement continued."The family are hopeful that the relevant authorities will do their upmost to get to the bottom of why our amazing son did what he did."A spokesperson for the South Yorkshire Police said Chapman's family are being supported by specialist officers.The incident, which took place shortly after 13:30 BST on Saturday, led to the evacuation and ongoing closure of the park.An eyewitness described seeing Chapman wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in.Mobile phone footage, believed to be from Chapman, appears to show the inside of the enclosure as he approaches the tiger across a patch of grass.Chapman was a former pupil of the Jackie Palmer Stage School in High Wycombe."We loved watching William grow, both as a person and as a performer, during his time with us," the Jackie Palmer Stage School in High Wycombe said in a tribute on Tuesday."It was a privilege to be part of his journey, and he will be remembered with great fondness by everyone who had the pleasure of knowing him.""Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with William's family and friends during this incredibly difficult time," the statement continued.As a child, Chapman appeared in the ITV production May Contain Nuts alongside Shirley Henderson - who is best known for playing Moaning Myrtle in the Harry Potter films - and Darren Boyd.He also portrayed Edward Jenner in the BBC series True Stories.Staff at Yorkshire Wildlife Park have separately said their "thoughts and heartfelt sympathies" are with Chapman's family and confirmed the rare Amur tiger, called Altai, remained in the enclosure and would not be euthanised.Dan Swaine, the local authority's executive director of place, said the council was "deeply saddened" by the incident and sent its "deepest sympathies" to Chapman's family and those who were at the scene.

schema.headline: Family pays tribute to 'warm and engaging' man killed in tiger attack
